question: A department wants Claude to take over a large slice of its quarterly reporting work. Which two steps belong before any full rollout? Select two.
options: A) Start with the reports carrying the highest legal exposure, since they save the most time.
B) Pilot the change on one report, so the result can be compared with the current output.
C) Agree what counts as an acceptable result before any of the work is handed over at all.
D) Announce the change as settled, so that the department commits to the new way of working.
E) Remove the existing review step first, so the pilot measures the fully automated version.
correct_answers: B) Pilot the change on one report, so the result can be compared with the current output.
C) Agree what counts as an acceptable result before any of the work is handed over at all.
explanations: Incorrect. Starting where legal exposure is greatest maximises the blast radius of a mistake in an untested process.
Correct. Piloting on a small scope gives a comparison against today's output before anything is committed department-wide.
Correct. Defining what good looks like before delegating is what makes the pilot's result interpretable at all.
Incorrect. Announcing the change as finished commits the department before there is any evidence the new way works.
Incorrect. Stripping review out of a pilot removes the safeguard exactly when the risk of an unnoticed error is highest.
